summary: Structure-based drug design utilizes target protein's three-dimensional structure to guide selection and modification of candidate ligands. Molecular docking proposes binding poses and assigns scores that help prioritize compounds. These scores are model-dependent estimates, not experimental measurements of binding affinity. A favorable docking score alone cannot establish therapeutic efficacy or safety. A hypothetical protein with a known binding pocket is considered for a computational study comparing a small ligand library across several protein conformations. The study examines hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, and steric clashes. Molecular dynamics simulations explore selected protein-ligand complexes over time. title: Structure-Based Drug Design: Test Research Note
